    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Alternating, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Matrices equal to the negative of their transpose #

    A matrix satisfying Mᵀ = -M is determined by its entries above the diagonal, once its diagonal is known to vanish: the entries below are the negatives of their mirror images. The diagonal does vanish as soon as the value ring has no element that is its own negative apart from zero, which covers every ring of odd characteristic.

    Main results #

    • Matrix.transpose_single_sub_single: transposing the difference of two opposite singleton matrices with the same coefficient negates it.
    • Matrix.transpose_map_of_transpose_eq_neg: the condition passes to the image of the matrix under an additive morphism of the entry types.
    • Matrix.diag_eq_zero_of_transpose_eq_neg: the diagonal vanishes when doubling is injective at zero, with Matrix.diag_eq_zero_of_transpose_eq_neg_of_charP reading that off an odd characteristic.
    • Matrix.trace_eq_zero_of_transpose_eq_neg: the trace vanishes when 2 is invertible.
    • Matrix.ext_of_lt_of_transpose_eq_neg: two such matrices with vanishing diagonals agree as soon as they agree above the diagonal.
    • Matrix.ofStrictUpper and Matrix.skewStrictUpperAddEquiv: complete arbitrary strict-upper entries and give additive coordinates when doubling has trivial kernel.
    • Matrix.ofStrictUpper_apply, Matrix.ofStrictUpper_zero, Matrix.ofStrictUpper_neg, and Matrix.ofStrictUpper_add: the entry formula and preservation of zero, negation, and addition.
    • Matrix.ofStrictUpper_apply_of_gt: lower entries are the negatives of the supplied upper entries.
    • Matrix.natCard_transpose_eq_neg: when doubling is injective at zero, the Nat.card of such matrices with entries in an additive subgroup I is (Nat.card I) ^ (k.choose 2), for an index type of cardinality k; for finite I this is the number of such matrices.

    (single i j a - single j i a).transpose = -(single i j a - single j i a)

          theorem Matrix.natCard_transpose_eq_neg {n : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [AddCommGroup S] (I : AddSubgroup S) (h2 : ∀ (x : S), x + x = 0 → x = 0) :
          Nat.card { M : Matrix n n S // (∀ (i j : n), M i j ∈ I) ∧ M.transpose = -M } = Nat.card ↥I ^ (Fintype.card n).choose 2

          Counting matrices equal to the negative of their transpose with entries in a subgroup. When zero is the only element that doubles to zero, such a matrix is determined by its entries above the diagonal, and these are arbitrary elements of the subgroup; for an index type of cardinality k there are k.choose 2 of them. As an identity of Nat.cards this holds for every subgroup; when the subgroup is finite it counts the matrices.
